definition: Sensual means richly pleasing or gratifying the physical senses.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word sensual. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know sensual should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: The resort's ads promise plainly sensual rewards: hot sand underfoot, cold juice at noon, and hammocks built for napping.
Comfortable is milder than sensual — comfort merely removes discomfort, while sensual pleasure actively delights the body.
Hedonistic goes further than sensual — sensual enjoyment savors the body's pleasures, while a hedonistic life is organized around chasing them.

Pleasurable covers any kind of enjoyment — a good book, a compliment, a solved puzzle all qualify. Sensual narrows the field to the body: pleasures of touch, taste, warmth, and ease. Praise can be pleasurable; a hot bath is sensual.

Indulgent is about permission: leaning into a pleasure past what is strictly needed, or letting someone else do so. Sensual is about the channel — the pleasure reaches you through the body's senses. A second dessert is indulgent; the taste of it is sensual.

Mara's guidebook chapter on the night market began as a list of stalls and prices, but her editor sent it back with one note: make the reader feel it.
So she rewrote the chapter as a walk, and the walk turned frankly sensual.
Steam from the dumpling carts settles on your forearms; grilled peaches hand you their smoke before you see the grill; the first bite of shaved ice lands as a small cold shock.
Her editor cut nothing this time, though he did note that not one sentence praised the market's history or its famous architecture.
That, Mara wrote back, was the point -- the chapter was about what the market does to a body, and the mind could take the week off.
